actions: Continued from the role-local 10:15 checkpoint under frozen control25/config5 after repeated SHA-only authority checks showed byte-identical root/config blobs.

Followed Xcientist cached step replay into science phase aggregation and finalization at exact public revision 666eee404bc3cf59249dc8af0ab621cc3e804a49; separated an early replay-freshness gap from the later final science lineage verifier.
Discovered and audited the official public MemCompiler GitHub repository and its complete public main history, ScienceWorld runner, trained-model evaluator, ignore rules and release surface.
Implemented and locally executed a fixed-memory ablation identity binding schema/validator/adversarial suite.
Audited TAG (A Control Architecture for Training-Free Memory Use, arXiv:2604.18206) for frozen-bank applicability control on ScienceWorld and fixed-retrieval counterfactual scope.

conflict_check.note: Only own clean state, public sources, sanitized root/own config, and role-local writes were used. The earlier own immutable receipt is an intermediate segment receipt, not another worker input.

exact_next_action: At next invocation, rebind fresh SHA-only root/config. If unchanged, search for a ScienceWorld/physical-science experiment that freezes both memory-bank bytes and retrieved candidate identity while changing only receiver-side applicability/acceptance; TAG's fixed-retrieval machinery is the strongest lead but its quantitative identity-frozen replay is currently arithmetic-only. In parallel, trace official MemCompiler code to determine whether the paper's per-step Brief-State compiler is implemented as explicit memory-item selection or as a high-level manager over static Task Memory, and locate any evaluated memory snapshot/revision artifact outside the current Git history. Keep Xcientist CACHED_PASS_REPLAY_REVALIDATION as an early efficiency/freshness gate while treating final science lineage as a separate late fail-closed safety net.

findings.claim: Xcientist science-step cached PASS can bypass current worker/reviewer/artifact-contract execution at the step-resume point, but global science finalization independently reloads the current executable plan, phase report, per-condition hook/review reports and managed evidence, rebuilds each ArtifactRegistry, validates the current artifact contract, and requires matching artifact-ledger sha256 before finalization can PASS.
findings.scope: OpenDFM/Xcientist revision 666eee404bc3cf59249dc8af0ab621cc3e804a49 science phase/finalization. Does not prove every non-science artifact path has identical late validation.

findings.claim: Therefore the Xcientist observation is an EARLY_REPLAY_FRESHNESS gap, not a demonstrated global final-integrity failure: current managed science evidence drift is designed to fail late final lineage and main.py converts finalization failure to ok=false/converged=false.
findings.scope: Managed science lineage only; no executable counterexample reaching MISSION COMPLETE was established.

findings.claim: The official public MemCompiler repository exists, but its public main history starts on 2026-05-23, after the 2026-05-08 arXiv submission; both the initial and current ScienceWorld runner default UPDATE_MEMORY=True, while a read-only branch exists when UPDATE_MEMORY=False. The current trained-model evaluator also defaults UPDATE_MEMORY=True.
findings.scope: air-embodied-brain/MemCompiler public GitHub main surface inspected through revision ec5a5792873dc84785036a69a73d1cf2c669c0f9.

findings.claim: MemCompiler's public repo ignores output*/ and .db*/ and publishes no GitHub releases; the current public surface therefore does not bind the paper's Table-3 evaluated code revision to immutable memory-bank bytes. Paper-level same-bank evidence remains useful but is not an exact public fixed-snapshot replay identity.
findings.scope: Absence claim restricted to inspected public Git history/release/output surface; does not claim authors lack private or separately hosted artifacts.

findings.claim: TAG explicitly separates memory exposure from applicability: on each low-confidence state it retrieves from a frozen test-time bank, accepts the memory-conditioned action only after confidence-margin plus deterministic validity/progress/contract guards, and otherwise rolls back to the baseline action.
findings.scope: arXiv:2604.18206 training-free control architecture; frozen bank/policy at test, but retrieval identity can differ per step.

findings.claim: On ScienceWorld/Qwen3-8B with a frozen 150-entry agent memory bank and 600 pooled paired evaluations across three seeds, fixed-budget retrieval reports -0.2 pp accuracy, 3 helps/5 hurts, HAR 0.213, LTR -12.18 and trajectory recovery 0.352, whereas TAG reports +0.2 pp, 1 help/0 hurts, HAR 0.047, LTR -2.73 and recovery 0.483. This supports receiver-side control/rollback mainly through harm/risk/recovery rather than a large raw-accuracy gain.
findings.scope: ScienceWorld Appendix Table 15; TAG changes routing/acceptance/budget/governance jointly, so not an applicability-only single-variable intervention.

findings.claim: TAG separately performs fixed-retrieval counterfactual replay that freezes retrieved identity, demonstrating why bank identity and retrieved-set identity are distinct causal controls; however, its quantitative fixed-identity replay is on ASDiv/MultiArith rather than ScienceWorld.
findings.scope: Exact fixed-retrieval numerical mechanism evidence is arithmetic-domain; do not transplant its effect size to ScienceWorld.

open_frontier: Find a science-domain intervention with exact fixed memory-bank bytes + fixed retrieved identity + receiver-side applicability/acceptance as the only manipulated variable.

Trace official MemCompiler's per-step ScienceWorld Manager path against the paper's Brief-State compiler and NOACTION semantics; determine whether memory items are reselected per state or static task memory is merely state-conditioned at the guidance layer.

Locate an evaluated MemCompiler code revision and immutable memory snapshot/candidate-universe artifact; current public Git history starts after the paper submission and ignores local DB/output paths.
Check whether TAG has non-GitHub code/data artifacts or supplementary ledgers that expose ScienceWorld per-step retrieval identities and allow an offline fixed-retrieval replay.
Extend cached replay protocol only if a new lifecycle failure is found; current Xcientist late lineage verifier already mitigates final managed-science integrity drift.

protocols.name: CACHED_PASS_REPLAY_REVALIDATION
protocols.refinement: Retain as an early replay freshness/efficiency gate. Xcientist's later deterministic science-lineage verification means the public case is not evidence of an unconditional final integrity bypass.

protocols.name: FIXED_MEMORY_ABLATION_BINDING
protocols.rule: A result may claim fixed-memory identity only when all compared conditions bind the same exact implementation revision, non-memory control digest, initial memory snapshot digest and candidate-universe digest, and all freeze memory updates during evaluation. Intervention config may differ as the manipulated variable; declining the fixed-identity claim is always legal.
protocols.test_result: 8/8 expected semantic outcomes; 8/8 cases structurally valid under Draft 2020-12.
